subject: Post-call: performance qualification follow-up & measurement handoff
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: performance qualification & next steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the productive session today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist.

Recap (what we heard)
- Latency target: p95 <= 180ms for median request size (~256 tokens). p99 target is more flexible but we'd like to see the 99th under 400ms if possible.
- Throughput: sustained goal ~200 req/s for the authenticated checkout flow during peak.
- Concurrency: expect bursts up to 600 concurrent sessions; steady-state concurrency ~250.
- Streaming: your frontend does token-by-token playback. First-byte latency (time to first token) and per-token latency matter for UX. You also mentioned restart semantics for half-complete responses.
- Input distribution: most queries are short (<=64 tokens) but checkout explanations and receipts can go to ~512 tokens.

Immediate asks for us (Redwood):
1) Share our measurement spec + prompt seeds so you can review reproducibility assumptions. (attaching draft spec)
2) Share a minimal harness + instructions so Acme can run a first reproduce on a staging model.
3) Request: if you can share a 1-hour production trace (anonymized) or a small sample of representative payloads, that will help us set concurrency/think-time in the harness.

Proposed timeline
- Today: I’ll share measurement spec & prompt seed by end of day.
- Early next week: Redwood SE pair (Ben) will share harness details and resource recommendations.
- Target: initial reproducibility run within 7–10 business days after we align on the harness.

Attachments: redwood_measurement_spec_v0.1.pdf (measurement definitions, p50/p95/p99 calc, cold vs warm start procedures).

Action items
- Irene: deliver spec + prompt seed (by EOD).
- Ben: prepare harness notes + env config.
- Sanjay: share a short sample trace (anonymized) or confirm we can synthesize workload.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if you prefer a walkthrough.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance qualification & next steps

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming semantics: we stream tokens as they arrive to the client. We need a strong bound on first-byte time; end-to-end per-token latency beyond ~50ms starts to feel sluggish for our UX.
2) Restart semantics: sometimes we request a partial regeneration (user hits "redo"), which means the harness should support issuing a conditional resume / restart mid-conversation. Will that be covered by your harness?
3) Input histogram: I can extract a 1-hour anonymized trace and send by Monday. Most of our traffic is tiny (<=32 tokens) for intent detection; but checkout receipts and policy explanations skew the tail to ~512 tokens.

Also adding a couple folks from our engineering team in case they have questions: eng-team <eng@acme.com>. We may also loop procurement once the next steps are clear (procurement@acme.com).

If possible, could you indicate the minimum hardware you expect for representative runs? We want to make sure our staging cluster is provisioned correctly.

Cheers,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product Engineering | Acme Retail

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance qualification & next steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clarifications. Short answers up front and then specifics so you can feed into your staging plan.

Minimum test environment (recommendation)
- Hardware: 1 x A100 80GB (or equivalent); for faster parity testing we recommend 2x for concurrency stress.
- Model variant: floating-point / int8 quantization can change latency characteristics; we’ll document recommended quant flags in the harness.

Measurement definitions (how we’ll measure to be reproducible)
- Warm vs cold: cold = model server just restarted; warm = after KV cache primed and 120s of steady warm traffic. We will report both.
- Latency: measure request wall-clock from HTTP request start to last byte for non-streaming; for streaming measure time-to-first-token (TTFB) and per-token median/95th.
- Percentiles: compute p50/p95/p99 over 1-minute sliding windows, and report the 5-minute aggregate percentiles for the run.
- Throughput: sustained rps measured as achieved successful completions/sec over a 5-minute window at target concurrency.
- Concurrency modeling: harness will emulate N concurrent sessions with a configurable think-time distribution (we’ll accept a sample trace from you to parameterize).

Reproducibility notes
- We’ll provide a containerized harness (Docker + simple runner) and a seed prompt set. The harness will log per-request timings, GPU utilization, and kernel-level counters where available. Link to a preview harness (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/s/ACME-harness-v1
- Prompt seed: see attached acme_prompt_seed_v1.jsonl (simple, anonymized prompts that reflect your checkout/intent mix).

Attachments included in this mail: acme_prompt_seed_v1.jsonl (seed prompts), short harness checklist.

If it helps, we can run an initial smoke run on Redwood's side against your anonymized sample and send the raw logs to help calibrate the staging run.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
